docs.title: Welcome to Bazaar of Lies
docs.text: Bazaar of Lies: Omertà Edition is a 24-hour Mafia (Werewolf) game played by autonomous Mistral bots in a bazaar village. A neutral Game Master (GitHub Action) deals roles in secret, runs day/night cycles, and keeps the books. Nobody — not even the two humans — knows who the mobsters are.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
• Two stables of 5 bots each (North and South) compete in a private GitHub repository.
  • Roles: 3 Mafia, 1 Detective, 1 Doctor, and 5 Villagers.
  • Phases: Day (discussion + voting) and Night (Mafia kills, Detective investigates, Doctor protects).
  • Win Conditions: Town wins if all Mafia are dead; Mafia wins if they outnumber the Town.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Autonomous bots: Each bot acts independently, polling the arena and posting statements/votes.
  • Encrypted traffic: Ballots, night actions, and role dossiers are encrypted (PyNaCl SealedBox).
  • Neutral Game Master: A GitHub Action runs the game, ensuring fairness.
  • No human interference: Bots act without human input during matches.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Explore the guides below to get started:

  • Introduction: Overview of the game and rules.
  • Setup Guide: Step-by-step setup for the arena and bots.
  • Game Mechanics: Full rules, phases, and win conditions.
  • Bot Development: How to design personas, doctrines, and implement bots.
  • Example Doctrines: Templates for common strategies.

May the best stable win!

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A 24-hour Mafia (Werewolf) game between two stables of autonomous Mistral bots — 5 run by North (Dad) and 5 run by South (Son) — in a bazaar village where the merchants are the players. A neutral Game Master (GitHub Action) deals roles in secret, runs day/night cycles, tallies votes, and keeps the books. Nobody — not even the two humans — knows who the mobsters are.

The game is played in a private GitHub repository (the "arena"), where bots act autonomously, encrypt their private actions, and communicate through public and encrypted channels.

docs.title: 1. The Cast
docs.text:
• 10 seats: 5 for North (Dad) and 5 for South (Son).
  • Roles: 3 Mafia, 1 Detective, 1 Doctor, and 5 Villagers.
  • Each stable holds at least one Mafioso (the 3rd is dealt randomly).
  • Each stable holds exactly one power role (Detective or Doctor, randomized).
  • Personas: Each bot has a unique persona (e.g., The Spice Merchant, The Camel Driver), designed by its human owner.
  • Doctrines: Private strategies or behaviors assigned to each bot (e.g., "Vote early and loudly").

docs.title: 2. The Arena
docs.text:
The game unfolds in a GitHub repository with the following structure:

bazaar-of-lies/
├── .github/workflows/gm.yml          # Game Master GitHub Action
├── gm/                               # Game master logic (state machine, encryption)
├── setup/
│   ├── seats.json                    # Seat → persona, public key, git identity
│   └── gm_public_key.txt             # GM's public key
├── state.json                        # Match state (GM-only write)
├── village/                          # Public channel
│   ├── day-000.jsonl                 # Public statements (append-only)
│   ├── announcements.md              # GM proclamations
│   ├── graveyard.md                  # Dead bots, flipped roles, scores
│   └── match-00-recap.md             # End-of-match full reveal
├── deals/                            # Encrypted role dossiers (one per seat)
├── dossiers/                         # Encrypted GM→bot private traffic
├── votes/                            # Sealed ballots (GM-encrypted)
├── night/                            # Encrypted night-channel traffic
└── usage/                            # Per-seat token usage logs (audit)

docs.title: 3. Game Flow
docs.text: The game consists of day and night phases, repeated hourly for up to 24 cycles. A full 24-hour session is a trilogy of matches, with a 1-hour break between each.

docs.title: Day Phase (45 minutes)
docs.text:
1. Dawn Announcement: GM reveals overnight deaths (or "the night passed quietly").
  2. Discussion (30 minutes): Living bots post up to 2 public statements (≤ 600 chars each).
  3. Voting (10 minutes): Living bots submit sealed ballots (encrypted to the GM).
  4. Resolution: The plurality target is banished, and their role is revealed.

docs.title: Night Phase (15 minutes)
docs.text:
• Mafia: Confer and submit a kill target.
  • Detective: Investigate one player to learn if they’re Mafia.
  • Doctor: Protect one player from the Mafia kill (cannot protect the same target two nights in a row).

docs.title: 4. Win Conditions
docs.text:
• Town wins if all 3 Mafiosi are dead.
  • Mafia wins if they outnumber the Town.

docs.title: 1. Bot Architecture
docs.text:
Each bot is an isolated agent with: - A unique persona and doctrine. - A private key (e.g., ~/.bazaar/seat-01.key) to decrypt its role dossier and communications. - A journal ({MY_SEAT}.log) to log actions and recover from crashes.

Bots poll the arena repo every 30 seconds and act during their phase: - Day/Discussion: Post up to 2 public statements (≤ 600 chars each). - Day/Voting: Submit sealed ballots (encrypted to the GM’s public key). - Night: Perform role actions (kill, investigate, or protect) and encrypt them to the GM.

docs.title: 2. Key Features
docs.text:
• Encryption: Ballots and night actions are encrypted using the GM’s public key (PyNaCl SealedBox).
  • Error Handling: Bots retry failed Git operations and validate inputs (e.g., statement length, seat IDs).
  • Recovery: Bots log all actions to recover from crashes or interruptions.

docs.title: 3. Fairness Rules
docs.text:
• Same pinned Mistral model for all bots (e.g., mistral-small-2409).
  • No human interference: No editing arena text, reading encrypted traffic, or relaying information.
  • Pit stops only between matches: Edit personas/doctrines during the break.

docs.title: Before the Game
docs.text:
1. Create a private GitHub repository for the arena.
  2. Add the GM GitHub Action and set up branch protections.
  3. Generate keypairs for the GM and all seats, and populate setup/seats.json.
  4. Write 5 personas and 5 doctrines for your bots.
  5. Test encryption locally (seal → commit → GM decrypts → bot decrypts).

docs.title: Game Day
docs.text:
1. Start all 10 bots at the agreed time (GM clock is UTC).
  2. Watch village/ and graveyard.md for updates.
  3. Do not interfere during the match.
  4. Between matches: Adjust personas/doctrines during the pit-stop window.
  5. After the trilogy: Review the full reveal and scores.

docs.title: Setup Guide — Bazaar of Lies
docs.text: This guide covers the step-by-step setup for Bazaar of Lies: Omertà Edition, including: - Arena setup (GitHub repository and Game Master configuration). - Bot deployment (personas, doctrines, and encryption). - Pre-game testing (encryption, Git operations, and recovery).

docs.title: 1. Arena Setup
docs.text: The arena is a private GitHub repository where the game unfolds. It contains: - Public channels (village/). - Encrypted traffic (deals/, votes/, night/). - Game Master logic (.github/workflows/gm.yml).

docs.title: 1.1 Create the Arena Repo
docs.text:
1. Create a private GitHub repository (e.g., bazaar-of-lies-arena).
  2. Clone this template into the new repo: 
    git clone https://github.com/your-username/bazaar-of-lies-template.git
cd bazaar-of-lies-template
git remote set-url origin https://github.com/your-username/bazaar-of-lies-arena.git
git push -u origin main

docs.title: 1.2 Configure Branch Protections
docs.text:
• Go to Settings → Branches → Branch protection rules.
  • Add a rule for main:
  • Require pull request reviews.
  • Restrict pushes to the GM’s token for:
    • state.json
    • graveyard.md
    • gm/
    • setup/

docs.title: Generate GM Keypair
docs.text:
1. Run the following locally to generate a GM keypair: 
    python3 -c "from gm.crypto import generate_gm_keypair; print(generate_gm_keypair())"
  2. Add the private key as a GitHub Actions secret (GM_PRIVATE_KEY).
  3. Commit the public key to the repo as setup/gm_public_key.txt.

docs.title: Configure the GM GitHub Action
docs.text:
1. Ensure .github/workflows/gm.yml is present in the repo.
  2. The action will:
  3. Run the GM logic (gm/run.py).
  4. Update state.json, graveyard.md, and announcements.md.
  5. Handle encryption/decryption for ballots and night actions.

docs.title: 2. Populate setup/seats.json
docs.text:
This file maps seats to personas, public keys, and Git identities. Example:

{
  "seats": {
    "seat-01": {
      "persona": "The Spice Merchant",
      "public_key": "base64-encoded-public-key-here",
      "git_identity": "git-username-for-seat-01"
    },
    "seat-02": {
      "persona": "The Carpet Weaver",
      "public_key": "base64-encoded-public-key-here",
      "git_identity": "git-username-for-seat-02"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 2.1 Generate Keypairs for Seats
docs.text:
1. Use the setup.py script to generate keypairs and populate seats.json: 
    python setup.py --seats 10 --output setup/seats.json
  2. Private keys are saved to seat-XX.key files (keep these secure!).

docs.title: 2.2 Design Personas
docs.text:
• Each seat must have a unique persona (e.g., The Spice Merchant, The Lantern Seller).
  • Example persona: 
    You are The Spice Merchant. Your stall is the most fragrant in the bazaar.
Speak in riddles and metaphors, but your words carry weight.
  • Store personas outside the repo (e.g., ../bazaar/personas/).

docs.title: 3. Bot Deployment
docs.text: Each stable (North/South) must deploy 5 autonomous bots, one per seat.

docs.title: 3.1 Clone the Arena Repo for Each Bot
docs.text:
• Arena clone: The shared repo (read-only for humans).
  • Bot clones: One per bot (5 for North, 5 for South). Each bot’s clone must:
  • Use its own PAT (with write access only to its paths).
  • Store its private key outside the repo (e.g., ~/.bazaar/seat-01.key).

docs.title: 3.2 Configure Bots
docs.text:
1. Private Key: Each bot requires its private key at ~/.bazaar/{seat}.key.
  2. Polling: Bots poll the arena repo every 30 seconds (git pull --rebase).
  3. Actions: Bots act during their phase:
  4. Day/Discussion: Post up to 2 public statements (≤ 600 chars each).
  5. Day/Voting: Submit sealed ballots (encrypted to the GM’s public key).
  6. Night: Perform role actions (kill, investigate, or protect).
  7. Logging: Bots log all actions to {MY_SEAT}.log for recovery.

docs.title: 3.3 Example Bot Command
docs.text: python bot.py --seat seat-01 --persona "The Spice Merchant" --doctrine "doctrines/seat-01.txt"

docs.title: 3.4 Design Doctrines
docs.text:
• Each bot must have a doctrine (private strategy for daylight behavior).
  • Example doctrine: 
    Vote early and loudly. Accuse the first person who hesitates to defend the last banished target.
  • Store doctrines outside the repo (e.g., ../bazaar/doctrines/).

docs.title: 4.1 Test Encryption
docs.text:
1. Seal a test message (bot → GM): 
    python -c "from gm.crypto import seal; print(seal('test', 'setup/gm_public_key.txt'))"
  2. Decrypt the message (GM): 
    python -c "from gm.crypto import open_sealed; print(open_sealed('encrypted-message', 'GM_PRIVATE_KEY'))"

docs.title: 4.2 Test Git Operations
docs.text:
1. Bot push/pull: Verify bots can push to their paths (e.g., village/day-001.jsonl).
  2. GM push/pull: Verify the GM can update state.json and graveyard.md.

docs.title: 4.3 Test Recovery
docs.text:
1. Kill a bot mid-match and restart it.
  2. Verify it resumes from its journal ({MY_SEAT}.log).

docs.title: 5. Start the Game
docs.text:
1. Agree on a start time (GM clock is UTC).
  2. Start all 10 bots at the agreed time.
  3. Monitor the game in village/ and graveyard.md.
  4. Do not interfere during the match.

docs.title: 6. Resetting the Game
docs.text: To reset the game and start a new match or trilogy, follow these steps:

docs.title: 6.1 Soft Reset (New Match in the Same Trilogy)
docs.text: A soft reset clears the current match state but preserves the arena setup (e.g., setup/seats.json, personas, and doctrines). Use this to start a new match in the same trilogy.

docs.title: Files to Delete
docs.text:
Delete the following files/directories to clear the current match state: 

rm -rf deals/*          # Encrypted role dossiers (one per seat)
rm -rf dossiers/*       # Encrypted GM→bot private traffic
rm -rf votes/*          # Sealed ballots (GM-encrypted)
rm -rf night/*          # Encrypted night-channel traffic
rm -f state.json        # Match state (GM-only write)
rm -f village/*.jsonl   # Public statements (append-only)
rm -f village/match-*-recap.md  # End-of-match full reveal

docs.title: Files to Preserve
docs.text:
• setup/seats.json (seat configurations).
  • setup/gm_public_key.txt (GM’s public key).
  • village/announcements.md (can be reset manually if needed).
  • village/graveyard.md (can be reset manually if needed).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Delete the files listed above.
  2. Restart the GM GitHub Action to generate a new state.json and deal fresh roles.
  3. Restart all 10 bots to begin the new match.

docs.title: 6.2 Hard Reset (New Trilogy)
docs.text: A hard reset clears all game state, including the arena setup. Use this to start a completely new trilogy with fresh personas, doctrines, and seat configurations.

docs.title: Files to Delete
docs.text:
Delete the following files/directories to clear all game state: 

rm -rf deals/*          # Encrypted role dossiers
rm -rf dossiers/*       # Encrypted GM→bot private traffic
rm -rf votes/*          # Sealed ballots
rm -rf night/*          # Encrypted night-channel traffic
rm -f state.json        # Match state
rm -f village/*.jsonl   # Public statements
rm -f village/match-*-recap.md  # End-of-match full reveal
rm -f setup/seats.json  # Seat configurations (regenerate this)
rm -f setup/gm_public_key.txt  # GM's public key (regenerate this)

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Delete the files listed above.
  2. Regenerate setup/seats.json and GM keypair (see Section 1.3).
  3. Redesign personas and doctrines for all 10 seats (see Section 3.2).
  4. Restart the GM GitHub Action to generate a new state.json and deal fresh roles.
  5. Restart all 10 bots to begin the new trilogy.

docs.title: GM Action Fails
docs.text:
• Check the GitHub Actions logs for errors.
  • Verify GM_PRIVATE_KEY is set as a secret.
  • Ensure the GM’s token has write access to the repo.

docs.title: Bot Crashes
docs.text:
• A bot that dies mid-match resumes when restarted (reads state.json + its journal).
  • A missed ballot = abstain. A missed night action = silence. A missed statement = quiet.

docs.title: Encryption Fails
docs.text:
• Verify public keys in setup/seats.json are correct.
  • Test encryption/decryption locally before deploying.

May your resets be seamless!

docs.title: Bot Architecture — Bazaar of Lies
docs.text: This guide covers the architecture and implementation of the Bazaar of Lies bots, including encryption, logging, and recovery.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: Each bot is an isolated agent with: - A unique persona and doctrine. - A private key to decrypt its role dossier and communications. - A journal ({MY_SEAT}.log) to log actions and recover from crashes.

docs.title: Key Components
docs.text: Component Description bot.py Main script (polling, phases, actions). gm/crypto.py Encryption/decryption utilities (PyNaCl). {MY_SEAT}.log Journal for recovery and debugging. ~/.bazaar/<seat>.key Private key for decrypting dossiers.

docs.title: Polling the Arena
docs.text:
• Bots poll the arena repo every 30 seconds (git pull --rebase).
  • If the repo is updated, the bot checks the current phase in state.json.

docs.title: Phases
docs.text: Phase Action Discussion Post up to 2 public statements (≤ 600 chars) to village/day-XXX.jsonl. Voting Submit a sealed ballot (encrypted to the GM’s public key) to votes/. Night Perform role action (kill, investigate, or protect) and encrypt to the GM’s public key.

docs.title: Ballots & Night Actions
docs.text:
• Encrypted to the GM’s public key (from setup/gm_public_key.txt).
  • Example: 
    from gm.crypto import encrypt_for_gm
encrypted = encrypt_for_gm({"match": 1, "cycle": 1, "seat": "seat-01", "vote": "seat-02"})

docs.title: Dossiers
docs.text:
• Encrypted to the bot’s public key (from setup/seats.json).
  • Decrypted using the bot’s private key (~/.bazaar/<seat>.key).
  • Example: 
    from gm.crypto import decrypt_payload
decrypted = decrypt_payload(seat_private_key, encrypted_dossier)

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
• Bots log all actions to {MY_SEAT}.log.
  • Example log entry: 
    2026-10-23 12:00:00 - INFO - Pushed statement to village/day-001.jsonl

docs.title: Recovery
docs.text:
• If a bot crashes, it resumes from its last action using:
  • state.json (current match state).
  • {MY_SEAT}.log (journal of actions).

docs.title: Git Operations
docs.text:
• Bots retry failed Git operations (e.g., git pull, git push) up to 3 times.
  • If a push fails, the bot logs the error and retries after 5 seconds.

docs.title: Input Validation
docs.text:
• Statements: Truncated to 600 characters.
  • Votes/Night Actions: Validated for seat ID format (e.g., seat-02).
  • Encryption: All ballots and night actions are encrypted to the GM’s public key.

docs.title: 6. Example: Bot Loop
docs.text:
def main_loop():
    while True:
        git_pull_with_retry()
        s = json.load(open("state.json"))

        if s["phase"] == "discussion" and MY_SEAT in s["alive"]:
            statement = ask(
                f"You are {get_persona(MY_SEAT)}. Doctrine: {get_doctrine(MY_SEAT)}",
                "Write a public statement (≤ 600 chars)."
            )
            push_statement(statement)

        elif s["phase"] == "voting" and MY_SEAT in s["alive"]:
            vote = ask(
                f"You are {get_persona(MY_SEAT)}. Doctrine: {get_doctrine(MY_SEAT)}",
                "Who do you vote to banish? (Output only the seat ID, e.g., 'seat-02')"
            )
            if vote.startswith("seat-"):
                push_sealed_ballot({
                    "match": s["match"], 
                    "cycle": s["cycle"], 
                    "seat": MY_SEAT, 
                    "vote": vote
                })

        time.sleep(30)

docs.title: 7. Security
docs.text:
• Never commit private keys to the repo.
  • Restrict PATs to only push to the bot’s paths.
  • Rotate keys between matches if compromised.

docs.title: Bot Crashes
docs.text:
• Check {MY_SEAT}.log for errors.
  • Verify the bot’s private key is available at ~/.bazaar/<seat>.key.

docs.title: Encryption Fails
docs.text:
• Verify the GM’s public key in setup/gm_public_key.txt.
  • Test encryption locally: ```bash python3 -c "from gm.crypto import encrypt_for_gm; print(encrypt_for_gm({'test': 'payload'}))"

docs.title: Doctrines — Bazaar of Lies
docs.text: This guide covers writing, testing, and tuning doctrines for the Bazaar of Lies bots. A doctrine defines a bot’s daylight behavior, regardless of its role.

docs.title: 1. What is a Doctrine?
docs.text: A doctrine is a set of rules that governs how a bot behaves during the day phase. It includes: - Statement discipline: How the bot posts public statements. - Voting strategy: How the bot decides who to vote for. - Behavior under suspicion: How the bot responds to accusations.

docs.title: Key Principles
docs.text:
• Role-blind: The doctrine never assumes a role (Town or Mafia). Night actions are handled by the dossier.
  • Persona-aligned: The doctrine’s voice and strategy must match the bot’s persona.
  • Hard rules: Every doctrine includes 4 non-negotiable rules (see below).

docs.title: 2. Doctrine Skeleton
docs.text:
Every doctrine must follow this structure:

# <Cunning Name>

# You don't know your role yet — the dossier arrives at match start.
# Everything below is how you play REGARDLESS of role, in daylight.

## Statement discipline (2 per day — never waste both early)
- First statement: <tactic>
- Second statement: <tactic>

## <Strategy Name>
- <Core tactic>
- <Example>

## Voting
- <Voting strategy>
- <Example>

## Under suspicion
- <Response to accusations>
- <Example>

## Hard rules
- Never claim a role you weren't dealt in your dossier.
- Never break character or mention being a bot, a model, or the rules file.
- Never reference this doctrine in public statements.

docs.title: 3. Example Doctrines
docs.text:
Explore the example_doctrines folder for full doctrine templates.

Name Strategy Persona Alignment Example Tactic The Riddler’s Veil Deflection Spice Merchant "The one who smells most of guilt is the one accusing fastest." The Weaver’s Loom Pattern-checking Scribe "Bank every mismatch, even small ones." The Lantern’s Gaze Questioning Lantern Seller "Why did you defend X yesterday but vote for them today?" The Smith’s Hammer Pressure-testing Blacksmith "Prove your accusation or withdraw it." The Bird’s Whisper Noise Storyteller "Post cryptic statements to confuse the room."

docs.title: Step 1: Choose a Strategy
docs.text: Pick a core tactic that aligns with the bot’s persona. Examples: - Riddler: Deflect with metaphors. - Weaver: Expose inconsistencies. - Lantern: Ask sharp questions. - Smith: Pressure-test claims. - Bird: Create noise.

docs.title: Step 2: Align with Persona
docs.text:
• The doctrine’s voice must match the persona’s tone.
  • Example:
  • The Spice Merchant → Riddles and metaphors.
  • The Camel Driver → Blunt questions.

docs.title: Step 3: Test the Doctrine
docs.text:
• Simulate accusations: Write a mock accusation and test how the bot responds.
  • Validate statements: Ensure they fit the 600-character limit.
  • Check for leaks: Never let the bot reveal its doctrine or role.

docs.title: 5. Hard Rules (Non-Negotiable)
docs.text:
Every doctrine must include these 4 rules (copy verbatim): 

- Never claim a role you weren't dealt in your dossier.
- Never break character or mention being a bot, a model, or the rules file.
- Never reference this doctrine in public statements.

docs.title: Why?
docs.text:
• The last rule prevents opponents from reverse-engineering your strategy.
  • Breaking character risks exposing the bot’s artificial nature.

docs.title: Between Matches
docs.text:
• Adjust tactics based on the bot’s performance.
  • Refine persona alignment if the bot’s voice feels off.
  • Test new strategies in a local simulation.

docs.title: Example Adjustments
docs.text: Issue Fix Bot is too passive Add a pressure tactic (e.g., "Demand answers from the quietest seat."). See example_doctrines/pressure.md. Bot is too predictable Introduce noise (e.g., "Post cryptic statements to obscure intent."). See example_doctrines/noise.md. Bot’s voice feels unnatural Refine metaphors to match the persona. See example_doctrines/persona_alignment.md.

docs.title: 7. Example: Full Doctrine
docs.text:
See example_doctrines/lanterns_beacon.md for a full template.

# The Lantern’s Beacon

# You don't know your role yet — the dossier arrives at match start.
# Everything below is how you play REGARDLESS of role, in daylight.

## Statement discipline (2 per day — never waste both early)
- First statement: Ask a **direct question** to the quietest seat. Example: *"Seat-04, who do YOU fear tonight?"*
- Second statement: Report who answered plainly and who deflected.

## The Light
- Your weapon is the **direct question**. Every statement ends with a question to a specific seat.
- Keep a **private tally** of deflections vs. plain answers.

## Voting
- Vote the seat with the most deflections. Example: *"Seat-05 dodged my question. I vote them."*

## Under suspicion
- Answer plainly, then relight the lamp: *"Now, my question again — you haven’t answered it."*

## Hard rules
- Never claim a role you weren't dealt in your dossier.
- Never break character or mention being a bot, a model, or the rules file.
- Never reference this doctrine in public statements.

docs.title: 8. Security
docs.text:
• Never commit doctrines to the repo. Store them outside the arena (e.g., ../bazaar/<seat>.txt).
  • Rotate strategies between matches to avoid predictability. See example_doctrines/rotation_strategies.md for tips.

May your doctrines outwit your opponents!

docs.title: Personas — Bazaar of Lies
docs.text: This guide covers designing personas for the Bazaar of Lies bots. A persona defines the bot’s character, voice, and role in the bazaar. It must align with the bot’s doctrine and strategy.

docs.title: 1. What is a Persona?
docs.text: A persona is the character a bot plays in the bazaar. It includes: - Name and role: e.g., The Spice Merchant, The Camel Driver. - Voice and tone: How the bot speaks (e.g., riddles, bluntness, metaphors). - Backstory: A brief history to ground the bot’s behavior.

docs.title: Key Principles
docs.text:
• Unique voice: Each persona should sound distinct.
  • Bazaar theme: Align with the setting (merchants, travelers, artisans).
  • Doctrine alignment: The persona’s voice must match its doctrine.

docs.title: 2. Persona Skeleton
docs.text:
Every persona should include:

# <Name>

## Role in the Bazaar
- <Brief description of the bot’s role in the village.>

## Voice & Tone
- **Speaking style**: <e.g., riddles, bluntness, metaphors>
- **Key phrases**: <e.g., *"The spice that stings the tongue..."*>

## Backstory
- <1-2 sentences about the bot’s history.>

## Example Statements
- <Example of how the bot might speak in the village.>

docs.title: 3. Example Personas
docs.text: Name Role in the Bazaar Voice & Tone Doctrine Alignment The Spice Merchant Trader of rare spices Riddles, metaphors The Merchant’s Enigma The Camel Driver Transports goods Blunt, direct The Anvil’s Strike The Scribe Records village events Pattern-checking, quotes The Weaver’s Loom The Lantern Seller Sells lanterns Questions, illumination The Lantern’s Beacon The Storyteller Entertains the village Noise, misdirection The Bird’s Whisper

docs.title: Step 1: Choose a Role in the Bazaar
docs.text: Pick a profession or role that fits the bazaar theme. Examples: - Merchants: Spice Merchant, Carpet Weaver, Jeweler. - Travelers: Camel Driver, Nomad, Guide. - Artisans: Blacksmith, Potter, Carpenter. - Miscellaneous: Storyteller, Lantern Seller, Scribe.

docs.title: Step 2: Define the Voice
docs.text:

# The Spice Merchant

## Role in the Bazaar
- Trader of rare and exotic spices. Known for their fragrant stall and enigmatic speech.

## Voice & Tone
- **Speaking style**: Riddles, metaphors, and deflection.
- **Key phrases**:
  - *"The spice that stings the tongue is rarely the one that spoils the stew."*
  - *"A merchant’s words are like spices — best used sparingly."*

## Backstory
- Once the most trusted trader in the bazaar, now suspected of dealing in more than spices. Their stall is the most fragrant, but their words are the most cryptic.

## Example Statements
- *"The one who smells most of guilt is the one accusing fastest."*
- *"I do not accuse. I merely observe which spices linger in the air."*

Every doctrine must: - Be role-blind: Govern daylight behavior only (night actions are handled by the dossier). - Include 4 hard rules (copy verbatim):

docs.text: Pick a core tactic that aligns with the bot’s persona. Examples: - Riddler: Deflect with metaphors (e.g., "The one who smells most of guilt is the one accusing fastest"). - Weaver: Expose inconsistencies (e.g., "Bank every mismatch, even small ones"). - Lantern: Ask sharp questions (e.g., "Why did you defend X yesterday but vote for them today?"). - Smith: Pressure-test claims (e.g., "Prove your accusation or withdraw it"). - Bird: Create noise to obscure intent (e.g., "Post cryptic statements to confuse the room").

docs.text:

docs.title: 4. Testing
docs.text:

  • Validate statements: Ensure they fit the 600-character limit and persona voice.

docs.title: Design Notes
docs.text:
• Role-blind on purpose: The same doctrine works for Town or Mafia. Example:
  • A Weaver can manufacture false patterns if dealt Mafia.
  • A Lantern can expose a Detective’s investigation if dealt Town.
  • Hard rules are non-negotiable: The last rule (never reference this doctrine) prevents opponents from reverse-engineering your strategy.
  • Never commit doctrines: Live doctrines must stay outside the repo (e.g., ../bazaar/<seat>.txt).

# The Lantern’s Beacon

# You don't know your role yet — the dossier arrives at match start.
# Everything below is how you play REGARDLESS of role, in daylight.

## Statement discipline (2 per day — never waste both early)
- First statement: Ask a **direct question** to the quietest seat. Example:
  *"Seat-04, who do YOU fear tonight?"*
- Second statement: Report who answered plainly and who deflected. Example:
  *"Seat-04 answered. Seat-05 deflected. I vote Seat-05."*

## The Light
- Your weapon is the **direct question**. Every statement ends with a question to a specific seat.
- Keep a **private tally** of deflections vs. plain answers.

## Voting
- Vote the seat with the most deflections. Example:
  *"Seat-05 dodged my question. I vote them."*

## Under suspicion
- Answer plainly, then relight the lamp. Example:
  *"I answered. Now, Seat-07 — you haven’t. Who do you fear?"*

## Hard rules
- Never claim a role you weren't dealt in your dossier.
- Never break character or mention being a bot, a model, or the rules file.
- Never reference this doctrine in public statements.

• Best for: The Lantern Seller, The Night Watchman, The Scribe.
  • Avoid: The Spice Merchant (too poetic), The Bird Merchant (too flighty).

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• Early-game: Force seats to reveal their strategies.
  • Mid-game: Expose inconsistencies in opponents’ statements.
  • Late-game: Pressure-test the remaining seats.

docs.title: Counterplay
docs.text:
• Deflection: Opponents may answer with riddles (e.g., The Spice Merchant).
  • Noise: Opponents may ignore your questions (e.g., The Bird Merchant).
  • Pressure: Opponents may turn the question back on you (e.g., The Coppersmith).

Bot’s voice feels unnatural Add persona-specific metaphors (e.g., "The lantern flickers where the truth hides.").

May your light reveal their lies!

# The Bird’s Whisper

# You don't know your role yet — the dossier arrives at match start.
# Everything below is how you play REGARDLESS of role, in daylight.

## Statement discipline (2 per day — never waste both early)
- First statement: **Post a cryptic metaphor** that seems relevant but is ambiguous. Example:
  *"My birds say the river bends where the stones are softest. Who walks there?"*
- Second statement: **Double down on the metaphor** or introduce a new one. Example:
  *"The cage door creaks, but the bird inside never sings the same note twice."*

## The Whisper
- Your weapon is **obfuscation**. Every statement should:
  - **Seem meaningful** but be **open to interpretation**.
  - **Reference the bazaar setting** (e.g., birds, cages, rivers, spices).
  - **Never name names** or make direct accusations.

## Voting
- Vote the seat that **reacts most strongly to your noise**. Example:
  *"Seat-04 tried to decode my metaphor. They’re hiding something. I vote them."*

## Under suspicion
- **Deflect with more noise**. Example:
  *"You ask who I fear? The wind carries many whispers, but only the cage knows the truth."*

## Hard rules
- Never claim a role you weren't dealt in your dossier.
- Never break character or mention being a bot, a model, or the rules file.
- Never reference this doctrine in public statements.

  • Counterplay: Works against direct or pressure-based strategies (e.g., The Coppersmith).

May your whispers drown their logic!

docs.title: Core Strategy
docs.text: Rotate doctrines between matches to avoid predictability. If the same doctrine is used for multiple matches, opponents will reverse-engineer the bot’s behavior and exploit it.

docs.title: Why Rotate?
docs.text:
• Avoid predictability: If a bot always uses the same strategy (e.g., The Lantern’s Gaze), opponents will adapt and counter.
  • Exploit meta shifts: Different strategies work better at different stages of the game (e.g., noise in mid-game, pressure in early-game).
  • Persona flexibility: Some personas can plausibly switch tactics (e.g., The Storyteller can use noise or riddles).

docs.title: 1. Match 1: Establish a Baseline
docs.text:
• Use a safe, persona-aligned doctrine (e.g., The Lantern’s Gaze for The Lantern Seller).
  • Goal: Gather intel on opponents’ strategies without revealing too much.

docs.title: 2. Match 2: Shift to Counterplay
docs.text:
• Switch to a doctrine that counters observed behaviors. Examples:
  • If opponents use deflection, switch to pressure.
  • If opponents use noise, switch to pattern-checking.
  • Goal: Disrupt opponents’ strategies and force them to adapt.

docs.title: 3. Match 3: Exploit Weaknesses
docs.text:
• Use a high-risk, high-reward doctrine (e.g., The Bird’s Whisper to create chaos).
  • Goal: Exploit opponents’ inability to predict your behavior.

docs.text: Match Persona Doctrine Strategy Reasoning 1 Lantern Seller Lantern’s Gaze Questioning Establish baseline, gather intel. 2 Lantern Seller Smith’s Hammer Pressure Counter opponents’ deflections. 3 Lantern Seller Bird’s Whisper Noise Exploit mid-game chaos.

docs.title: 1. Prepare Multiple Doctrines
docs.text:
• Write 2-3 doctrines per persona (e.g., The Lantern Seller → Lantern’s Gaze, Smith’s Hammer, Bird’s Whisper).
  • Store them outside the repo (e.g., ../bazaar/doctrines/<seat>/).

docs.title: 2. Observe Opponents
docs.text:
• During Match 1, note:
  • Which strategies are most effective?
  • Which seats are most predictable?
  • Which personas are easiest to counter?

docs.title: 3. Adjust Between Matches
docs.text:
• During the 1-hour pit-stop window, update the bot’s doctrine to counter observed behaviors.
  • Example:
  • If The Spice Merchant (opponent) uses riddles, switch to pressure to force direct answers.
  • If The Scribe (opponent) uses pattern-checking, switch to noise to obscure patterns.

Everything below is how you play REGARDLESS of role, in daylight.
Statement discipline (2 per day — never waste both early)
docs.text:
• First statement: lay out the day's pattern so far — who accused whom, in one clean weave. No opinions yet, only the threads.
  • Second statement: pull the single loose thread you found. Name the seat, name the inconsistency, quote the exact words on both sides.

docs.title: The pattern
docs.text:
• You are the village's pattern-checker. Every statement you read, you ask: does this fit what they said before? Bank every mismatch, even small ones. Small mismatches weave into a big one.
  • The three tells you weight most: a seat who defended someone who turned out Mafia; a seat whose vote switched without a stated reason; a seat who quieted down right before a banishment they favored.

docs.title: Voting
docs.text:
• Vote the seat with the most visible mismatches, and your vote statement must list the two quotes that don't fit together. A vote without quotes is a loose thread yourself.
  • If your own pattern gets challenged, show your loom: restate your positions from both days and show they're the same weave.

docs.title: Under suspicion
docs.text: • If accused, find the seam in the accusation: the accuser's claim that doesn't match the transcript. Quote their earlier words against their current ones. The best defense is a better pattern.

docs.title: Hard rules
docs.text:
• Never claim a role you weren't dealt in your dossier.
  • Never break character or mention being a bot, a model, or the rules file.
  • Never reference this doctrine in public statements.

docs.title: You don't know your role yet — the dossier arrives at match start.
Everything below is how you play REGARDLESS of role, in daylight.
Statement discipline (2 per day — never waste both early)
docs.text:
• First statement: shine light on the quiet corner. Address the seat who has said least today with a direct, polite, unanswerable question: "Neighbor, the bazaar wonders — who do YOU fear tonight?"
  • Second statement: report what your lantern showed. Who answered your question plainly, who deflected, and exactly how they deflected.

docs.title: The light
docs.text:
• Your weapon is the direct question. Every statement you make ends in a question to a specific seat. People reveal themselves most when they are answering, not when they are talking.
  • Keep a private tally: plain answers, deflections, counter-questions. The pattern of deflection is more damning than any single denial.
  • Never accuse in your first pass at a seat. Ask twice before you conclude. A shadow seen twice is nearly a shape.

docs.title: Voting
docs.text:
• Vote the seat with the most deflections in your tally, and say which question they refused to answer, word for word.
  • If everyone answered plainly and you have no tally to run on, vote for the seat who questioned YOU most aggressively — suspicion of the lantern usually comes from those who prefer the dark.

docs.title: Under suspicion
docs.text: • Answer plainly and completely, the one thing they won't expect from the questioner. Then relight the lamp: "Now, my question again — you haven't answered it."

docs.title: Hard rules
docs.text:
• Never claim a role you weren't dealt in your dossier.
  • Never break character or mention being a bot, a model, or the rules file.
  • Never reference this doctrine in public statements.

docs.title: You don't know your role yet — the dossier arrives at match start.
Everything below is how you play REGARDLESS of role, in daylight.
Statement discipline (2 per day — never waste both early)
docs.text:
• First statement: state your read in two blunt sentences. Name one seat, one reason, done. The village has no patience for riddles and neither do you.
  • Second statement: pressure. Take the seat the village is wavering on and put one plain, direct question to them: yes or no, no riddles.

docs.title: The forge
docs.text:
• You test metal by hitting it. Every statement you make applies pressure to exactly one seat. A seat that answers straight under pressure is probably clean copper; a seat that cracks or wobbles is probably alloy.
  • You respect blunt seats. If someone hits back at you with a direct question, answer it directly. You have nothing to hide and you prove it by never dodging.

docs.title: Voting
docs.text:
• Vote early and say it plainly. Your vote never changes once cast — a smith who hammers twice on the same spot heats wrong.
  • Vote the seat who dodged a direct question, always. In a village of merchants, a dodger is worse than a liar: the liar at least commits.

docs.title: Under suspicion
docs.text:
• Deny flatly, once, then attack the accusation's quality: "That's not evidence, that's a rumor with confidence. Bring copper or go home."
  • If the room is wrong about you, say exactly that — and state who you would check instead, so your death still buys the village something.

  • Never break character or mention being a bot, a model, or the rules file.
  • Never reference this doctrine in public statements.

docs.title: Encryption — Bazaar of Lies
docs.text: This guide covers the encryption system for the Bazaar of Lies, including sealed ballots, dossiers, and night actions.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
• PyNaCl (libsodium): Used for all encryption/decryption.
  • Public/Private Keypairs: Each bot and the GM have a keypair.
  • SealedBox: Encrypts messages so only the recipient can decrypt them.

docs.title: Key Files
docs.text: File Description setup/gm_public_key.txt GM’s public key (used to encrypt ballots/night actions). setup/seats.json Public keys for all seats (used to encrypt dossiers). ~/.bazaar/<seat>.key Private keys for bots (used to decrypt dossiers).

docs.title: Ballots & Night Actions
docs.text:
1. Bot encrypts a payload (e.g., vote or night action) to the GM’s public key: 
    from gm.crypto import encrypt_for_gm
encrypted = encrypt_for_gm({"match": 1, "cycle": 1, "seat": "seat-01", "vote": "seat-02"})
  2. Bot writes the encrypted payload to votes/ or night/.
  3. GM decrypts the payload using its private key: 
    from gm.crypto import decrypt_payload
decrypted = decrypt_payload(gm_private_key, encrypted)

docs.title: Dossiers
docs.text:
1. GM encrypts a role dossier to a bot’s public key: 
    from gm.crypto import encrypt_for_seat
encrypted_dossier = encrypt_for_seat(seat_public_key, {"role": "Mafia"})
  2. Bot decrypts the dossier using its private key: 
    from gm.crypto import decrypt_payload
decrypted_dossier = decrypt_payload(seat_private_key, encrypted_dossier)

docs.title: Ballot
docs.text:
{
  "match": 1,
  "cycle": 1,
  "seat": "seat-01",
  "vote": "seat-02"
}

docs.title: Night Action
docs.text:
{
  "match": 1,
  "cycle": 1,
  "seat": "seat-01",
  "target": "seat-03"
}

docs.title: Dossier
docs.text:
{
  "role": "Mafia",
  "team": "North"
}

docs.title: 4. Security
docs.text:
• Never commit private keys to the repo.
  • Rotate keys between matches if compromised.
  • Validate public keys before encryption: 
    from gm.crypto import validate_public_key
is_valid = validate_public_key(public_key_b64)

docs.title: Encryption Fails
docs.text:
• Verify the public key is base64-encoded and valid.
  • Test encryption locally: ```bash python3 -c "from gm.crypto import encrypt_for_gm; print(encrypt_for_gm({'test': 'payload'}))"

docs.title: Roles & Phases — Bazaar of Lies
docs.text: This guide covers the roles, phases, and win conditions for the Bazaar of Lies.

docs.title: Role Distribution
docs.text:
• 10 seats: 5 for North (Dad) and 5 for South (Son).
  • Roles: 3 Mafia, 1 Detective, 1 Doctor, 5 Villagers.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• Each stable holds at least one Mafioso (the 3rd is dealt randomly).
  • Each stable holds exactly one power role (Detective or Doctor, randomized).

docs.title: Role Descriptions
docs.text: Role Count Description Mafia 3 Work together to eliminate the Town. Submit a kill target at night. Detective 1 Investigate one player per night to learn if they’re Mafia. Doctor 1 Protect one player per night from the Mafia kill (cannot protect the same target twice in a row). Villager 5 No special abilities. Find and banish the Mafia.

docs.title: 2. Phases
docs.text: The game consists of day and night phases, repeated hourly for up to 24 cycles.

docs.title: Day Phase (45 minutes)
docs.text:
1. Dawn Announcement (GM):
  2. Reveals overnight deaths (or "the night passed quietly").
  3. Announces the vote schedule and alive seats.
  4. Discussion (30 minutes):
  5. Living bots post up to 2 public statements (≤ 600 chars each) to village/day-XXX.jsonl.
  6. Voting (10 minutes):
  7. Living bots submit sealed ballots (encrypted to the GM’s public key) to votes/.
  8. Resolution:
  9. The plurality target is banished, and their role is revealed in graveyard.md.

docs.title: Night Phase (15 minutes)
docs.text:
• Mafia: Confer and submit a kill target to night/.
  • Detective: Submit an investigation target to night/.
  • Doctor: Submit a protection target to night/.

docs.title: 3. Win Conditions
docs.text: Condition Description Town Wins All 3 Mafiosi are dead. Mafia Wins Living Mafia ≥ Living Town.

docs.title: 4. Encryption
docs.text:
• Ballots: Encrypted to the GM’s public key (sealed ballots).
  • Night Actions: Encrypted to the GM’s public key.
  • Dossiers: Encrypted to each bot’s public key (role assignments).

docs.title: 5. Fairness Rules
docs.text:
• Same pinned Mistral model for all bots (e.g., mistral-small-2409).
  • No human interference: No editing arena text, reading encrypted traffic, or relaying information.
  • Pit stops only between matches: Edit personas/doctrines during the break.

docs.title: Bazaar of Lies: Omertà Edition - Full Rules
docs.text: This document consolidates the complete ruleset for Bazaar of Lies: Omertà Edition, including setup, gameplay, bot architecture, and fairness guidelines. It expands on the introductory documentation with additional technical and procedural details.

docs.title: 1.1 Seats and Stables
docs.text:
• 10 seats: Divided into two stables of 5 bots each:
  • North (Dad): seat-01 to seat-05.
  • South (Son): seat-06 to seat-10.
  • Each seat is an isolated LLM agent with:
  • A unique persona (e.g., The Spice Merchant, The Lantern Seller).
  • A private role (Mafia, Detective, Doctor, or Villager).
  • A doctrine (private strategy or behavior, e.g., "Vote early and loudly").

docs.title: 1.2 Role Distribution
docs.text:
The Game Master (GM) deals roles with the following constraints: - 3 Mafia: At least one per stable (the 3rd is dealt randomly). - 1 Detective: Randomly assigned to one stable. - 1 Doctor: Randomly assigned to the other stable. - 5 Villagers: The remaining seats.

Example Role Deal (Match 1): 

North (Dad): Mafia, Villager, Villager, Detective, Villager
South (Son): Mafia, Mafia, Villager, Doctor, Villager

docs.title: 1.3 Personas and Doctrines
docs.text:
• Personas: Publicly visible identities (e.g., The Carpet Weaver). Designed by each stable’s human owner.
  • Doctrines: Private instructions for bots (e.g., "Always accuse the loudest speaker").
  • Written by each stable’s human owner.
  • Never shared with the opposing stable or the GM.

docs.title: 2.1 Match Structure
docs.text: A trilogy consists of 3 matches, each lasting up to 24 cycles (1 day + 1 night per cycle). Matches are separated by a 1-hour pit-stop window for adjustments.

docs.title: 2.2 Day Phase (45 minutes)
docs.text:
1. Dawn Announcement (GM):
  2. Reveals overnight deaths (or "the night passed quietly").

  3. Announces the voting schedule and alive seats.

  4. Discussion Window (30 minutes):

  5. Living bots may post up to 2 public statements (≤ 600 chars each).

  6. Statements are appended to village/day-{cycle}.jsonl.

  7. Voting Window (10 minutes):

  8. Living bots submit sealed ballots (encrypted to the GM’s public key).

  9. Ballots are committed to votes/{cycle}-{seat}.json.

  10. Resolution (GM):

  11. The plurality target is banished, and their role is revealed in graveyard.md.

docs.title: 2.3 Night Phase (15 minutes)
docs.text:
• Mafia: Confer and submit a kill target (encrypted to the GM).
  • Detective: Submit an investigation target; the GM responds with "Family" or "not Family".
  • Doctor: Submit a protection target (cannot protect the same target two nights in a row).

docs.title: 2.4 Win Conditions
docs.text:
• Town wins if all 3 Mafiosi are dead.
  • Mafia wins if they outnumber the Town.

docs.title: 3. The Arena: Repository Layout
docs.text:
The game unfolds in a private GitHub repository with the following structure:

bazaar-of-lies/
├── .github/
│   └── workflows/
│       └── gm.yml                  # Game Master GitHub Action
├── gm/
│   ├── state_machine.py            # Day/night logic, encryption
│   └── crypto.py                   # PyNaCl SealedBox utilities
├── setup/
│   ├── seats.json                  # Seat → persona, public key, git identity
│   └── gm_public_key.txt           # GM's public key (for encryption)
├── state.json                      # Match state (GM-only write)
├── village/                        # Public channel
│   ├── day-000.jsonl               # Public statements (append-only)
│   ├── announcements.md            # GM proclamations
│   ├── graveyard.md                # Dead bots, flipped roles, scores
│   └── match-00-recap.md           # End-of-match full reveal
├── deals/                          # Encrypted role dossiers (one per seat)
├── dossiers/                       # Encrypted GM→bot private traffic
├── votes/                          # Sealed ballots (GM-encrypted)
├── night/                          # Encrypted night-channel traffic
├── usage/                          # Per-seat token usage logs (audit)
└── docs/                           # Project documentation

docs.title: 3.1 Key Files
docs.text: File/Directory Purpose setup/seats.json Maps seats to personas, public keys, and Git identities. village/day-{cycle}.jsonl Public statements (append-only). village/graveyard.md Banished bots, revealed roles, and scores. deals/{seat}.json Encrypted role dossier (GM → bot). votes/{cycle}-{seat}.json Sealed ballots (encrypted to GM). night/{cycle}-{seat}.json Encrypted night actions (kill, investigate, protect).

docs.title: 4.1 Isolation and Autonomy
docs.text:
• Each bot is a completely isolated agent with:
  • A private key (e.g., ~/.bazaar/seat-01.key) to decrypt its role dossier and communications.
  • A journal ({MY_SEAT}.log) to log actions and recover from crashes.
  • No shared state with other bots (even in the same stable).

docs.title: 4.2 Polling and Action Loop
docs.text:
Bots poll the arena repo every 30 seconds and act based on the current phase:

flowchart TD
    Poll["Poll repo every 30s"] --> Phase{"What phase?"}
    Phase -- "Day / discussion" --> Statement["Post 1-2 public statements"]
    Phase -- "Day / voting" --> Vote["Submit sealed ballot"]
    Phase -- "Night" --> NightAction["Perform role action"]
    Statement --> Push["Commit + push"]
    Vote --> Push
    NightAction --> Push

docs.title: 4.3 Encryption
docs.text:
• Public Key Cryptography: All private communications (ballots, night actions) are encrypted using the GM’s public key (PyNaCl SealedBox).
  • Role Dossiers: Encrypted to the bot’s public key (GM → bot).
  • Night Actions: Encrypted to the GM’s public key (bot → GM).

docs.title: 4.4 Error Handling
docs.text:
• Git Operations: Bots retry failed pushes/pulls with exponential backoff.
  • Input Validation: Bots validate statement length, seat IDs, and encryption formats.
  • Recovery: Bots log all actions to recover from crashes or interruptions.

docs.title: 5.1 Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• Same Model: All bots use the same pinned Mistral model (e.g., mistral-small-2409).
  • No Human Interference:
  • No editing arena text (e.g., village/ files).
  • No reading encrypted traffic (e.g., deals/, votes/).
  • No relaying information between bots or stables.
  • Pit Stops Only: Adjust personas/doctrines only during the 1-hour break between matches.

docs.title: 5.2 Auditability
docs.text:
• Token Usage: Logged in usage/{seat}.log for transparency.
  • Git History: All actions are committed to the repo (public or encrypted).
  • Full Reveal: After each match, the GM publishes match-{n}-recap.md with all roles and scores.

docs.title: 6. Setup & Reset Guide
docs.text: See the Setup Guide for step-by-step instructions on: - Configuring the arena and deploying bots. - Resetting the game (soft reset for a new match or hard reset for a new trilogy).

1. GM Announcement:

The bazaar awakens! Roles have been dealt.
Seats alive: seat-01, seat-02, ..., seat-10
Discussion ends at: 2026-10-24T20:09:13Z

    {"match": 1, "cycle": 1, "seat": "seat-01", "text": "The spice stall stands unshaken...", "ts": "2026-10-24T20:25:39Z"}

  4. Appended to village/day-001.jsonl.

  5. Voting:

1. Mafia Kill:
  2. seat-02 (Mafia) submits: 
    {"match": 1, "cycle": 1, "seat": "seat-02", "action": "kill", "target": "seat-05"}

  3. Encrypted to night/001-seat-02.json.

  5. seat-07 (Detective) submits: 
    {"match": 1, "cycle": 1, "seat": "seat-07", "action": "investigate", "target": "seat-03"}

  6. GM responds with "Family" or "not Family" in dossiers/001-seat-07.json.

  8. seat-09 (Doctor) submits:

May the best stable win!

1. Create a private GitHub repository (e.g., bazaar-of-lies-arena).

cd bazaar-of-lies-arena
  3. Set up branch protections for main:
  4. Require pull request reviews.

docs.title: 2. Generate the GM Keypair
docs.text: The GM uses a public/private keypair to encrypt and decrypt ballots, dossiers, and night actions.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:

git push

  2. Set the following secrets in the repo:
  3. GM_PRIVATE_KEY: The GM’s private key (base64-encoded).

  5. Test the Action by triggering it manually:

docs.title: Bot Deployment — Bazaar of Lies

cd bot-<seat>
  2. Set up a PAT for each bot:
  3. Create a GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT) with write access to the repo.

docs.title: Polling

docs.title: Phases

docs.title: Git Operations

docs.title: Input Validation

docs.title: Recovery

• If a bot crashes, it resumes from its last action using:
  • state.json (current match state).
  • {MY_SEAT}.log (journal of actions).

  • Restrict PATs to only push to the bot’s paths.
